findings: Both primary comparisons completed on the same 56 sequences (84,274 response tokens), with zero optimizer updates and verified matching learner/serving parameters. Mean absolute log-probability disagreement rose from 0.05719 at checkpoint 384 to 0.17820 at checkpoint 512 (3.12-fold). The fraction of token probabilities differing by more than 2× rose from 1.827% to 7.641%. Aggregating the paired archive texts for each question, disagreement increased on all 28 questions and all 14 categories.

Forcing the learner to use vLLM’s response expert choices reduced mean disagreement by 65.4% at checkpoint 384 and 70.8% at checkpoint 512. Large disagreements fell to 0.234% and 1.683%, respectively. The intervention reduced the mean gap on all 28 questions at each checkpoint, and recorded expert-set agreement under replay was 100%. Native expert-set disagreement increased more modestly, from 17.55% to 19.24% of measured token/layer positions. The much larger probability effect is consistent with increased sensitivity to routing differences; the experiment does not identify its first numerical trigger.

The checkpoint-by-text comparison shows a strong interaction. On archive-384 text, the gap rose from 0.04069 to 0.24132. On archive-512 text, it instead fell from 0.08514 to 0.07131. Thus the aggregate increase is driven by the later checkpoint becoming especially inconsistent on earlier response traces. A claim that agreement worsened uniformly on all text would be incorrect. The fixed-token experiment demonstrates a persistent checkpoint-dependent effect, while also showing that response content substantially changes its size.
limitations: This establishes a causal contribution of response-route selection to the probability mismatch in this diagnostic. It does not establish that the mismatch caused the task-accuracy regression; that requires a controlled training comparison. Fresh restores do not reconstruct the original in-memory serving state. These jobs used GB200 hardware and new physical placements, whereas the training run used H100s.

The panel is small and family-balanced, with responses capped at 2,048 tokens. Prompt routes remain native during replay. The residual gap is comparable to repeat/rebatch variation within a backend, but is not zero and can still include prompt-routing effects. The optional decode control at checkpoint 384 failed before generation, after its complete primary comparison had been saved; the checkpoint-512 control completed.
decode_control: At checkpoint 512, 32 generated responses to four questions supplied 7,896 scored tokens and 30 distinct response-token sequences. All requests used the shared seed 20261017; repeated prompts are not treated as independent samples. This control uses the probabilities and expert routes recorded during actual autoregressive decoding.

Relative to the decode probabilities, the learner’s mean absolute log-probability gap fell from 0.06365 to 0.02258 under response-route replay (a 64.5% reduction). The fraction of probability ratios outside ½–2 fell from 2.166% to 0.823%; k3 fell from 0.03797 to 0.00773. This supports the routing mechanism on actual generated tokens, beyond the archived-text prefill comparison.

vLLM prefill rescoring itself differed from vLLM decoding: mean absolute log-probability difference 0.05242, with 1.938% of ratios outside ½–2. Execution-mode sensitivity therefore also matters. The fixed-panel k3 values are especially tail-sensitive: one token contributes 56.7% of checkpoint 512’s native k3, and one token contributes 98.8% of the separate fresh-restore vLLM control’s k3. These descriptive statistics must not be interpreted as current-policy KL or as task accuracy.
